item.content: {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=intrinsic+constraints+goal+formation+autonomous+objectives&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"The effects of parental psychological control and career decision-making self-efficacy on college students' employment anxiety: the mediating role of motivational regulation.\", \"abstract\": \"Employment anxiety has become an important issue affecting college students' psychological well-being and career development, yet its underlying mechanisms require further investigation. Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study examined associations of parental psychological control and career decision-making self-efficacy on college students' employment anxiety, and further explored the mediating roles of identified regulation and external regulation. A questionnaire survey was conducted among 509 junior undergraduate students facing the upcoming graduation and job-search period. Participants completed the Future Employment Anxiety Scale, Parental Psychological Control Scale, Career Decision-Making Self-Efficacy Scale, and Work Extrinsic and Intrinsic Motivation Scale (WEIMS). Structural equation modeling and the Bootstrap method were employed to examine the relationships among the variables. The results showed that: (1) Parental psychological control was significantly and positively associated with college students' employment anxiety, whereas career decision-making self-efficacy significantly and negatively associated with employment anxiety in statistical prediction; (2) Parental psychological control was significantly and negatively associated with identified regulation and external regulation, while career decision-making self-efficacy was significantly and positively associated with both types of motivational regulation; (3) Identified regulation and external regulation served as parallel statistical mediators in the associations between parental psychological control, career decision-making self-efficacy, and employment anxiety; and (4) Further analysis revealed that both types of motivational regulation showed masking patterns opposite to the directions of the direct statistical effects, suggesting that different forms of motivational regulation may be simultaneously l…
